newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STRETCHED BY GERMAN PROSPECT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STRETCHED BY GERMAN PROSPECT.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras struggled to his second win in 16 hours at the Swiss indoor championships on Thursday.
Playing in his first tournament since winning the U.S. Open, Sampras narrowly overcame German wild card entry Tommy Haas 6-4 2-6 6-3.
Sampras looked only marginally sharper against Haas than he did in his first round match against another hard-hitting German Alex Radulescu, who also forced him to three tough sets.
The American made a quick start against Haas. He broke his opening serve then went on to claim the first set.
But Haas, rated by many to be the best German prospect since Boris Becker, came back to dominate the second set. He broke Sampras to go up 4-2 and repeated it to close out the set.
In the third set, Sampras showed the player ranked 219 in the world, that he still has much to learn. Sampras broke him three times to finish the match and reach Friday's quarter-finals.

"I got off to a good start, I had a solid first set," said Sampras, who beat Haas when they met for the first time in Indianapolis last month. "He (Haas) was a lot more comfortable out there than the last time I played him.
"After the second set I was upset with myself because I couldn't close it out. I think in the third set it was experience that came through."
Sampras, looking fit and rested after his break, denied reports that he was suffering from anaemia.
"It's all speculation," he said. "Whoever wrote that didn't know what they were talking about. It was just his opinion why I was getting tired on court.
"The fact is it's just conditioning. It's getting near the end of the year and it's not what it should be."
